description: Composite figure of three panels, of which the caption names only (a) and (b); a third unlabelled panel follows. (a) is a dark-field TEM micrograph of the 0.001% P steel (Fe-30Mn-9Al-1Si-0.9C-0.5Mo, aged 0.5 h at 570 °C) imaged with a ⟨100⟩_κ κ-carbide superlattice reflection: a very high number density of tiny bright ordered domains (~few unit cells) in a dark matrix. A 10 nm scale bar sits at lower left and a selected-area diffraction pattern with an arrow-marked objective aperture/beam stop is inset at upper right. (b) is the equivalent dark-field image of the 0.043% P steel: bright domains are distinctly larger, brighter and locally arranged in rows, with a 25 nm scale bar and its own inset diffraction pattern — the different scale bars mean the two micrographs were recorded at different magnifications, so sizes cannot be compared from the pixels alone. (c) is an unlabelled false-colour 2D map with tick labels -30, -20, -10, 0, 10, 20, 30 on both axes (unit and axis titles absent), showing smooth blue-to-yellow/red fluctuations with no colour bar. Together the group argues that phosphorus increases the size and number density of κ-carbide ordered domains.
measured_quantities: scale bar length (nm): 10 nm in (a), 25 nm in (b)
map axis coordinate range (arbitrary units, -30 to 30)
ordered domain size (nm, stated in citing text as 5 nm average for the high-P steel)

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a dark-field TEM micrograph with a 10 nm scale bar and a selected-area diffraction inset marked by a dark arrow, showing a high number density of very fine bright ordered domains in a dark matrix.

Panel (b) is a dark-field TEM micrograph with a 25 nm scale bar and its own inset diffraction pattern, showing larger and brighter domains than (a); the two panels use different scale bars (10 nm vs 25 nm), so their magnifications differ.
The third, unlabelled panel is a false-colour 2D map whose x and y axes are tick-labelled -30, -20, -10, 0, 10, 20, 30 with no axis titles, no units and no colour bar.
No numeric size value, composition value or data label is printed anywhere on the micrographs; only the scale bars (10 nm and 25 nm) and the map tick labels are legible numbers.

The caption states that the dark-field images are of the (a) 0.001% P and (b) 0.043% P steels aged for 0.5 h at 570 °C, and that the size and number density of κ-carbides appear greater with increasing phosphorus.
The citing text states that Figure 4 shows dark-field TEM ⟨100⟩_κ images of a 0.001% P and a 0.043% P Fe-30Mn-9Al-1Si-0.9C-0.5Mo steel aged 0.5 h at 570 °C.

The citing text states that the low-phosphorus steel contains a high number density of small (a few unit cells in dimension) ordered domains with diffraction intensity corresponding to the perovskite crystal structure of κ-carbide.
The citing text states that in the high-phosphorus steel the ordered domains are much larger, at an average size of 5 nm, and are preferentially coarsening along ⟨100⟩_κ.

The citing text states that phosphorus greatly increases the size and volume fraction of κ-carbide precipitation and accelerates both the first-stage ordering reaction and concurrent spinodal decomposition.

The citing text states that phosphorus was found to be randomly distributed between the matrix and the κ-carbide, so the increased hardening rate with phosphorus is not related to long-range diffusion of phosphorus, but instead to an increased rate of spinodal decomposition during aging at 530 °C (shown in Fig. 5).

The caption asserts that the number density of κ-carbides appears greater with increasing phosphorus, which the pixels can only support qualitatively because (a) and (b) were recorded at different magnifications (10 nm vs 25 nm scale bars).

subfigures.description: Dark-field TEM micrograph of the 0.001% P steel aged 0.5 h at 570 °C, taken with a ⟨100⟩_κ κ-carbide reflection: numerous very fine bright ordered domains dispersed in a dark matrix. Scale bar 10 nm at lower left; SAED pattern inset at upper right with a dark arrow (objective aperture/beam stop) and several sharp spots.

Dark-field TEM micrograph of the 0.043% P steel under the same aging condition: brighter, visibly larger ordered domains, some aligned into short rows/strings. Scale bar 25 nm at lower left; inset diffraction pattern at upper right with a bright central beam and satellite spots.

Unlabelled false-colour 2D field map, both axes tick-labelled -30, -20, -10, 0, 10, 20, 30 (units not given), displaying smooth continuous fluctuations from blue (low) through green to yellow/red (high) maxima; no colour bar, axis title or panel letter is visible.
